questions.text: A group member gives an answer that misreads the passage. What does the rubric reward the leader for doing next?
options: Correcting them at once so nobody is confused
Asking the group what the verse itself says
Moving on to keep the session on time
Explaining the right reading in a short talk

questions.text: What is the clearest sign of Scripture engagement in a session?
options: The leader quotes many verses from memory
People read the passage aloud and point to it when they answer
Everyone brings a different translation
The session covers a whole book

questions.text: Which question is most likely to lead to application?
options: What city was Paul writing to?
What does this passage say about God?
Where in your week does this verse ask something of you?
Who wrote this letter?

questions.text: What does a healthy session structure usually look like?
options: It starts with the hardest question
It opens, reads, discusses, applies and closes in prayer, with time kept for each
It leaves prayer out when time runs short
It lets the discussion run until people leave

questions.text: After the passage has been read aloud, what should the leader usually do first?
options: Ask the hardest question straight away
Wait a few seconds and let the group take it in
Give a summary of what it means
Move on to prayer requests

questions.text: Why does Coach look at structure and flow at all?
options: To reward leaders who finish exactly on time
Because a predictable shape frees the group to focus on the text and on each other
Because longer sessions score higher
To rank leaders against each other
